join_order.notes: Scan info_type.info varlen (113 rows) via memcmp to obtain target_it_id once.
memmem scan over keyword.dat (134170 rows); expected handful of matches. For each kid, walk CSR offsets[kid..kid+1] to collect candidate movie_ids.

join_order.build: candidate_movies (hash_set of movie_ids from CSR probe)
join_order.notes: Use dense PK: production_year_bin[movie_id]. Filter y != INT32_MIN && y > 1990. Keep survivors as a vector<int32_t> sorted ascending (movie_id order) to maximize sequential mi_idx access.

For each surviving mv: lo=off[mv], hi=off[mv+1]; iterate r in [lo,hi); require info_type_id_bin[r]==target_it_id and lex compare mi_idx.info > '2.0'. mi_idx is FK-sorted by movie_id so probes are sequential.

data_structures.candidate_movies: absl-style flat_hash_set<int32_t> sized for ~20k entries, then drained to sorted vector<int32_t>
data_structures.aggregation: two scalar accumulators: best_mi_info (string_view), best_title (string_view); lex-min via memcmp

parallelism.notes: Parallelize (a) keyword memmem scan over 134170 rows by row-range morsels, (b) per-movie mi_idx range scan + aggregation over the sorted surviving_movies vector by movie-index morsels. Each thread keeps a local (best_mi_info, best_title) pair, reduced at end via lex memcmp. info_type scan is trivially serial.

indexes.purpose: join_lookup: kid -> mk row positions -> movie_ids
